# Measuring Bicycle Chain Wear

Use a ruler, not feel. A new chain measures exactly 12 inches across 12
links, pin to pin. When the same span reads 12 and 1/16 inches, the chain
has stretched 0.5 percent and should be replaced on an 11-speed drivetrain;
at 12 and 1/8 inches you have likely worn the cassette teeth too and will
need both parts.

Replacing a 25-euro chain on schedule saves the 90-euro cassette. A worn
chain rides higher on each tooth and files the tooth profile into a hook
shape, which is why a new chain skips on an old cassette under load.

Check every 500 kilometers in dry weather and every 300 in winter, since
road grit mixed with wet lube works like grinding paste on the rollers.
